opening.quote: could afternoon, thank your for calling titwell Home, brown speaking. How can I so help you?
opening.comment: The greeting gives the agent's name (Brown) and the company name (Tidewell Home), though the transcript is garbled and the caller's greeting is attributed to the customer turn, so it is hard to be certain; the agent name and company are present in the first turn.

verification.quote: I've updated account to efa.smit@example.com. Your order confirmations will there.
verification.comment: The agent changed the account email and then discussed the order without confirming the caller's full name plus order number or account postcode first.

understanding.quote: Sure, happys to help with that. What's this new email address?
understanding.comment: The agent captured the request to change the email and the order status question, and did not re-ask for information already given.

resolution_accuracy.quote: your lamp shipped morning and arrives in 3 to 1 working this.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The delivery timeline is garbled and does not match the standard 2 to 4 working day policy, and the email was also recorded as efa.smit instead of eva.smit, which is an inaccurate account change.

process_compliance.comment: No hold or damaged-item steps applied, but the agent mis-recorded the customer's email address, so the account update was not handled accurately.

communication.comment: The caller was not shown to be frustrated, so no acknowledgement was needed, but the closing response was abrupt and unclear.

closing.comment: The agent did not confirm next steps or ask if there was anything else, and ended the call abruptly.
